name: Hodgkin-Huxley space-clamped membrane driven by a held current
question: Which functions of the history of an injected current does the membrane potential represent?

provenance.source: A. L. Hodgkin and A. F. Huxley, J. Physiol. 117, 500-544 (1952), Eqs. (7), (12)-(16), (20)-(26), Table 3 (values chosen), doi:10.1113/jphysiol.1952.sp004764

assumptions: the source convention: V is the displacement from rest in mV, depolarization negative; Iext is the membrane current density I of Eq. (26) in uA/cm2, inward positive, so a depolarizing injected current is Iext < 0 (the name I is reserved by the parser)
temperature 6.3 C, so phi = 1 (the rate expressions as printed)
the input Iext is redrawn for every interval of 1 ms and held within it (not in the source, which applies shocks and constant currents)
the observable is V, measured at the end of each interval (or at virtual_nodes times within it)

drift.V: (Iext - gK*n**4*(V - VK) - gNa*m**3*h*(V - VNa) - gl*(V - Vl))/CM
